steps.content: The destination of this walk is in sight—a small camp. It doesn't look like a base camp for the expedition, probably just a temporary base for an investigative squad.
But there is something in the camp that makes you hold your breath—

You see a huge <color=#fb9259>mech</color>, very similar to the behemoth you saw in the contamination. The only difference is that this one is unfinished with many half-assembled parts. Overall it's less broken, and some parts are quite new.
When you're up against a monster, you're facing its present, past, and future selves all at once. Each and every version of it is an independent entity.
Are they the same mech? Could this thing also become the center of a temporal storm in the future? Can people from this spacetime go to your era through it? What should you do?
You should ask, but... in what capacity?
You can't recognize it? You've seen the prototype at the base, it was only as tall as you then.
The woman who saved you skillfully removes her armor and stands beside you with a toolbox. Now she just looks like an ordinary woman, much less intimidating.
The question slips out, then you realize it might sound weird when you see her frown. According to your "dreams" from before, they seem to see you as some kid...?
Ow... my head, what happened, where is this? Did... I forget something? My head... hurts so bad...
The woman looks serious and examines your head. After making sure there are no serious injuries, she reaches into her pocket and stuffs a biscuit in your hand.
You have three bumps on your head. That was pretty scary for you, right? You're safe now. I'm Vanilla, your teammate, the logistician, and mechanic of the team.

steps.speaker: Vanilla
steps.content: I came here with a small investigation team. We set up a temporary camp here.

steps.speaker: Vanilla
steps.content: Yes, that's me.

steps.speaker: Vanilla
steps.content: The others are all out investigating. Our plan is to investigate the nearby temporal storm and evaluate its dangers.
What about you...

steps.speaker: Vanilla
steps.content: I'm no researcher, I'm the team's logistician, protecting the camp is my job.

steps.speaker: Vanilla
steps.content: All the research data, the reserves, and provisions are all here. If I left my post, monsters would swarm in and destroy all their hard work.

steps.speaker: Vanilla
steps.content: And you? Why did you come here all alone?

steps.speaker: Vanilla
steps.content: This place is far from the main camp, and it's dangerous near the temporal storm. There's no one with you?
You think for a moment.

options: There are, we came here for you.

steps.content: I'm the guide. Finding people and places is my job, so I came to find you. And I'm not alone this time.
There are many teammates outside. I'm just... a scout. I came here to recon the place first, and then I'll figure out how to bring you back.
We can start now. I'll go scout, and we'll leave as soon as possible!
Your lie doesn't raise any suspicion, but it does puzzle her a bit. After some thought, Vanilla answers.

steps.speaker: Vanilla
steps.content: ...Maybe I didn't make myself clear. Let me explain again... The temporal storm has moved and taken control of this camp and its surrounding area. It's very dangerous outside. Until the storm subsides, we can't leave.

steps.speaker: Vanilla
steps.content: They're not the problem. The real danger of the temporal storm is that time becomes unreliable. We can no longer accurately "observe" time.
Seeing how perplexed you look, Vanilla thinks for a moment, takes out a pocket watch, and slowly explains while organizing her thoughts.

steps.speaker: Vanilla
steps.content: Take this pocket watch as an example. When you're looking at it, or rather, observing it, its time moves forward with you, second by second. This is reliable time. It allows you to correctly perceive the world.

steps.speaker: Vanilla
steps.content: But in the storm, if you fall asleep, faint, or lose consciousness and are unable to observe just for a split second, this pocket watch could jump to another random time state when you look again.

steps.speaker: Vanilla
steps.content: It could be the past, or the future where it's all rusty or no longer exists. I'm not just talking about this pocket watch, the whole world operates this way. If your time is no longer in sync with the world, it could destroy your mind in some severe cases.

steps.speaker: Vanilla
steps.content: I'm being very serious right now. Remember, it's way more dangerous than the misty mazes you usually encounter. You mustn't let yourself be in a situation where this might happen, got it?
She tries to look as stern as possible to emphasize the seriousness of the situation. You cover your eyes and loudly count to 10, then open them to look at the pocket watch.
You watch as the second hand ticks once, indicating a total of 11 seconds have passed.

steps.speaker: Vanilla
steps.content: I should explain more... Observation isn't just about seeing with your eyes. It's also about your consciousness and focus—what you're thinking about. That's what "observation" in the DisSea is.

steps.speaker: Vanilla
steps.content: ...Forget it, this might be too nerve-wracking for you.
You smile.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I think you're really strong. That big guy, you built it, right?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: If we can complete it, perhaps we can break through that horde of monsters, with all the research materials and supplies in the camp!
Vanilla lifts her head, frowns slightly, but remains silent.

You squint your eyes. The bandage wrapped around her right leg is soaked with blood, and there's a stick for support. It could be a fracture, or a large open wound. Either way, it's not an injury that can heal quickly.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Hmm... It must be difficult to build such an enormous machine alone, especially with your injury. But now that I'm here...
You glance at Vanilla's injured leg.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I'm no good at building stuff, but I can help you collect materials. On the way here, I saw several abandoned settlements. There must be something useful there.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I'll be careful and stay away from the storm or the monsters. You've taught me the ropes too—I'll run as soon as I see a monster.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I promise to only search around the camp. If something is wrong, I'll come back right away. I won't be in any danger.
Vanilla stares into your eyes, letting out a faint sigh.

steps.speaker: Vanilla
steps.content: ...Do you really want to leave that much?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I have to find a way out.
After a short silence, Vanilla finally budges:

steps.speaker: Vanilla
steps.content: Okay. I'll prepare everything for you tomorrow. Sleep now. You need rest.

options: It's okay, I'm not tired. I don't need rest.

steps.content: You sit across from Vanilla, watching as she works. This is "observation," right?
Although you're not quite sure what the temporal storm thing is all about, it wasn't easy to get here and meet her. You don't want to fall asleep and "jump" to somewhere else.
But watching her, a sense of tranquility washes over you. You don't feel as tense, and after you loosen up, your eyes gradually...
